newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst sees steady 97 operating profit.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst sees steady 97 operating profit.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG said on Wednesday its 1997 operating profit would likely not show a marked difference from the one reported for 1996.
For 1996 Hoechst reported an operating profit of 4.013 billion marks, up from 3.591 billion marks reported in 1995.
Hoechst chief executive Juergen Dormann told a news conference "I do not expect a marked difference," when asked about the outlook for the operating profit.
But Dormann cautioned that last year's figures could no longer be used for direct comparisons as they do not accurately reflect a number of spin-offs completed last year.
The group's chief financial officer Klaus-Juergen Schmieder said that Hoechst currently set the exchange rate for the U.S. dollar at 1.55 marks, the same level used in 1996.
He said any 10 pfenning rise in the dollar would then translate into a 100 million mark gain in operating profit or a 50 million mark gain in pre-tax profit.
But Schmieder too cautioned against extrapolating future results from these statements as the base numbers would be changed considerably through the various divestments.
